clue.text: Extreme party people: not a piece of cake remaining!

parts.note: a piece of cake is something easy, so not one is hard
what is remaining is left over

explanation.surface: Someone laments that the whole cake has been eaten by guests at an extreme party.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads like a complaint about greedy guests; in fact it splits into two plain synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard left are the radical socialist wing of a political party, its extreme members.

clue.text: One used to carry fare: bacon rolls with mash

indicators.note: rolls suggests tumbling over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A café serves bacon rolls with mashed potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like food, matching bacon rolls and mash; it means a paying passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire carried paying passengers in Victorian streets.

clue.text: Stick doctor next to old composer

parts.note: a rod is a stick
to rig is to doctor or falsify, as in rigging an election

explanation.surface: A doctor with a walking stick stands next to an elderly composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb here, meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Joaquín Rodrigo was the Spanish composer of the Concierto de Aranjuez.

clue.text: Spooner's partly abbreviated name for harmonica player

indicators.note: partly abbreviated means one part of the name is cut to its initial

parts.note: Larry Adler was a famous American harmonica virtuoso

explanation.surface: Reverend Spooner gives a shortened, muddled name for a harmonica player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner' screams Spoonerism, but there is no swap: the first name cut to its initial and run into the surname gives the word, and a Spooner here is literally someone using a spoon. The 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who ladles serves with a big spoon, so a person spooning out food is a ladler.

clue.text: A scream following weapon's appearance in madhouse

parts.note: something that is a scream is hilarious, funny
F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A scream rings out after a weapon appears in an asylum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' reads as a link of order but it supplies F, the abbreviation used in 'p. 12 f'.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny farm is old slang for a psychiatric hospital, like madhouse.

clue.text: Miss Piggy's outside reflecting in a low voice

indicators.note: in places the turned pair of letters inside the word for a low voice

parts.note: a bass is the lowest male singing voice

indicators.note: reflecting, like a mirror, says the pair of letters is turned round
outside asks for the outer letters of the word Piggy

explanation.surface: Miss Piggy, the Muppet, admires her reflection while speaking in a deep voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Piggy' reads as the Muppet's name, but 'Miss' alone is the definition; 'reflecting' turns the outer pair and 'in' places them inside the low voice.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to go round it and avoid it, so to miss it out.

clue.text: In cracking bone, upset dish

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: cracking means first-rate, A1, written here as A and I
a rib is a bone

explanation.surface: Someone upset a dish while cracking a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' looks like breaking the bone, but it means excellent: A1, read as AI. IN AI RIB turned upside down by 'upset' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Biriani is a South Asian dish of spiced rice cooked with meat or vegetables.

clue.text: Jack in supporting post incurs penalty, maybe

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means sitting underneath, so this piece comes second

parts.note: to post someone somewhere is to place them
to jack in a habit is to give it up, to kick it

explanation.surface: A jack is wedged into a supporting post and someone is penalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack in' is British slang for quit, the same as 'kick' a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A penalty in rugby may be taken as a kick at goal with the ball placed on the ground.

clue.text: Elegant writer putting pen to paper for shopper?

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
a shopping list is a piece of paper a shopper carries

explanation.surface: An elegant writer puts pen to paper to note what a shopper needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool alongside 'writer', but it is an enclosure for pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylist is a writer admired for the polish and elegance of their prose style.

clue.text: Green light put on wheels

indicators.note: wheels suggests turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: Someone is given the go-ahead to put something on wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' reads as part of the surface phrase 'put on wheels', but it is the signal to turn DON round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nod is a sign of approval or permission, just as a green light is the go-ahead.

clue.text: Adult female attending courses at school

definitions.text: Adult female attending courses at school

parts.words: Adult female attending courses at school
parts.note: reads like a mature student, but the courses are the parts of a meal and the woman serves them at lunchtime

explanation.surface: A grown woman goes back to school to study.
explanation.walkthrough: Courses here are not lessons but parts of a meal. In Britain a school canteen worker is commonly called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who serves school lunches works alongside the meal's courses at a school.

clue.text: Loves lively, original, animated girlfriend

indicators.note: animated means lively and moving, and original means newly made, so the letters are set in a fresh order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O; two loves give two
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lively girlfriend is praised for being original and full of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated' also points to the cartoon world: she is Popeye's sweetheart. The letters O, O and LIVELY are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Popeye cartoons she is the sailor hero's long-standing sweetheart.

clue.text: A team's outside left skipping second half to see girl?

indicators.note: outside says the outer letters wrap round the shortened word

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals, with the possessive S kept

indicators.note: skipping its second half keeps only the opening half of the word left

explanation.surface: A team's outside left player skips the second half of a game to go and see a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside left' looks like a football wing position, but 'outside' is the container signal and 'left' is the word halved by 'skipping second half'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexis is a given name used for women, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Jam or Clash's Number One record

indicators.note: Number One is the top of the pile, so it asks for the first letter of the word Clash

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether The Jam or The Clash had a number one record.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jam and The Clash were both British punk-era bands, which disguises 'Jam' as a band name rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To clog a pipe is to jam or block it, so the two verbs share a sense.

clue.text: Barking dog won't, if found out

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the letters are sent crazy

explanation.surface: A barking dog won't stop if someone finds out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' fits the dog but works as the British slang for mad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To get wind of something is to learn of it, especially by hearing rumours.

clue.text: Group supporting Charles I's chasing victory in board game

indicators.note: in puts the victory and the following letters inside the name of the game

parts.note: darts is a game played by throwing at a board

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a victory is a win
I's read as I is, giving the letters as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Charles celebrates a win at a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles is not a king here but Charles Darwin, the naturalist. 'Darts' is a pub game played with a dartboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Charles Darwin's theory of evolution form a group backing his ideas.

clue.text: Be ecstatic to have minor sort of part on show

parts.note: a walk-on is a small non-speaking role in a play
to air something is to show or broadcast it

explanation.surface: An actor is thrilled to land a small part in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to a theatre part; the part is literally a walk-on and 'show' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk on air is an idiom for feeling elated and happy.

clue.text: One not going to bed in suit is ultimately warmer without I see

definitions.text: One not going to bed in suit

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word is
without here means outside, so the kinder word goes round the others

parts.note: kinder means more warm-hearted, warmer
taken as written
V is the abbreviation of vide, Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps in a suit because it is warmer without it, they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is the seabed, and 'suit' a diving suit; this diver goes down without one. 'without' means outside, an old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin diver swims underwater without a full diving suit, often near the surface.

clue.text: Call in bar — sort providing non-alcoholic drink

indicators.note: in places the word for call inside the other two pieces joined

parts.note: bar means except, as does but
ilk means kind or sort
to term something is to call it by a name

explanation.surface: Someone calls in at a bar and the barman provides a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' wants to be a pub, which suits the drink; it means 'except'.
explanation.definitionFit: The liquid left after churning butter is drunk as a soft, alcohol-free drink.

clue.text: Ruling woman being inferior, not qualified to be Speaker

indicators.note: being inferior in a down clue means placed below, so this comes after

parts.note: utter means absolute, without qualification
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A ruling woman is judged inferior and not qualified to be Speaker of the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests the Commons role, but means anyone who speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who utters words, who says them, is a speaker in the plainest sense.

clue.text: Weird sorcerer producing rifle

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or weird
a mage is a magician or sorcerer

explanation.surface: A weird sorcerer conjures up a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun but is a verb: to search through.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through drawers is to search hurriedly, to root about.

clue.text: From the east, hail a Korean screen goddess

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading from right to left
a screen conceals, so the answer lies concealed in the words before it

explanation.surface: A Korean film star is greeted as a screen goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screen goddess' looks like one phrase for a film star; 'screen' signals the concealed letters, and 'From the east' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Kali is a Hindu deity, the fierce goddess of time and destruction.

clue.text: A pair lie without energy, being pessimistic

parts.note: a pair is two

indicators.note: without means the letter for energy is dropped

parts.note: to rest is to lie down
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A couple lie around listlessly, feeling gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means lacking, so E comes out of REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'at worst' gives the gloomiest estimate, the pessimistic view of an outcome.

clue.text: Are there times when a tip goes round?

indicators.note: goes round says the outer pieces encircle the letters for times

parts.note: a tip is an end, as of a finger
T is an abbreviation for time; two of them stand for times

explanation.surface: Someone wonders when the waiter's tip will be shared round.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as one sentence; 'Are there' is the definition, and the rest is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to be present, so people who attend an event are there.

clue.text: Hall in university getting a tidy round

indicators.note: round says the joined words go around the letter for university

parts.note: trim means neat or tidy

explanation.surface: A university hall gets a tidy-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in university' reads as the hall's location; 'round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is the central hall or open court of a building, a grand entrance space.

clue.text: Showed deference — or anything due — when following king

indicators.note: when following means the other pieces come after the letter for king

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
owt is northern English dialect for anything
what is due is owed

explanation.surface: Someone bowed before the king out of what they felt was owed.
explanation.walkthrough: OWT is a dialect word from northern England meaning 'anything' (its opposite is NOWT, nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: To kowtow is to kneel and bow low, an act of extreme deference in old Chinese custom.

clue.text: English speaker holding a CD back gets one in a pickle

indicators.note: back says the whole assembly is read in reverse order
holding means the talker's word contains the other pieces

parts.note: a gabber is someone who talks a lot, a speaker
taken as written

explanation.surface: An English public speaker holds a compact disc while in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts A CD inside the talker, 'back' turns the whole thing to read REDCABBAG, then E follows. 'in a pickle' means in trouble, but is literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Red cabbage is a vegetable commonly preserved in vinegar, so a jar of it sits in pickle.

clue.text: Minister's brief to produce spin

definitions.meaning: the short form of Reverend, a title given to clergy
to make an engine turn faster, as in racing it

explanation.surface: A government minister's brief is to produce spin.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a political minister and press spin; the minister is a clergyman and 'brief' means abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Rev abbreviates Reverend, a clergyman's title, and to rev an engine is to make it spin faster.

clue.text: Touch filter in need of repair

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A water filter needs fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch' looks like a verb but is a noun: a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle means a little, as in 'a trifle cold', just as a touch does.

clue.text: Come before tailless golden eagle, say

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to predate is to come earlier than
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A golden eagle without a tail flies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golden eagle' reads as the bird's name, but 'golden' gives OR, the heraldic term for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a bird of prey, an example of a hunting animal.
